registeredBy: Sam (owner) chose to pre-register G23 before the tool is built (efficient build order, 2026-11-09); registered before any run and before the runner exists
hypothesis: A country-quarter in which the BIS credit-to-GDP gap is above 10 percentage points (the Basel III countercyclical buffer threshold; Drehmann and Juselius 2014) is followed by the start of a systemic banking crisis in that country within the next 12 quarters more often than country-quarters in general.

data.signal: BIS credit-to-GDP gap (WS_CREDIT_GAP, series C), as the app already reads it
data.outcome: Start year of a systemic banking crisis, Laeven and Valencia (2018, IMF Working Paper 18/206), Table of crisis dates; a crisis start year counts from its first quarter
data.universe: Every country with both a BIS credit gap and a Laeven-Valencia record

sample.to: last crisis-date year in the Laeven-Valencia file

knownLimits: The Laeven-Valencia dates end in 2017 in the 2018 update; no crises after that are scored unless a newer edition is read (a newer edition would be a new version of this test).
Systemic crises are rare and many start in 2007-2008, so the result leans on one global episode; resampling whole years counts that cluster as one block, not many.

The BIS gap is a one-sided HP filter (lambda 400,000), but the series on file is today's vintage: credit and GDP revisions since each quarter are not removed. The two-quarter release lag is applied on top.
Quarters already inside a crisis are left out, so the test asks about onsets only.
Licence for the Laeven-Valencia file not confirmed (IMF working paper; no dataset terms found on 2026-11-11). The runner is built only once the licence row is settled.
